req.title: Create new post
req.statement: The system shall insert a new post attributed to the logged-in user when POST /create receives a title and body, then redirect to /.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /create with a title and body, when the user is logged in, must insert a post row attributed to that user and return a 302 redirect to /. I design: (1) a positive EP test confirming the happy path inserts the row and redirects; (2) a negative NEG/DT test confirming that a missing title causes no insert and flashes an error (no redirect); (3) a boundary BVA test with a single-character title (minimum non-empty boundary) to confirm it is accepted; (4) a STC test confirming that an unauthenticated user is redirected to /auth/login instead of creating a post; (5) a DT test confirming that an empty body with a valid title still inserts (body is optional per source). Each test uses exact status codes, exact redirect locations, and verifies DB state directly to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_create_post_happy_path_inserts_row_and_redirects
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing seed data
User Rahul (id=1) is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /create with title='Test Title' and body='Test body content'
expected: A new row exists in the post table with title='Test Title', body='Test body content', author_id=1
trace: R-FLASKR-015: POST /create with title+body inserts row and redirects to /
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Test Title', 'body': 'Test body content'})
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute(
        "SELECT title, body, author_id FROM post WHERE title = 'Test Title'"
    ).fetchone()
    assert row is not None
    assert row['title'] == 'Test Title'
    assert row['body'] == 'Test body content'
    assert row['author_id'] == 1

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    count_before = db.execute(
        'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post WHERE author_id = 2'
    ).fetchone()[0]

r = client.post('/create', data={'title': '', 'body': 'Some body'})
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'Title is required.' in r.data

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    count_after = db.execute(
        'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post WHERE author_id = 2'
    ).fetchone()[0]
    assert count_after == count_before

preconditions: App initialised with test database containing seed data
No user is logged in (fresh client session)
actions: POST /create with title='Unauthorized Post' and body='body' without logging in
expected: No new post row is inserted
trace: R-FLASKR-015: unauthenticated state — login_required decorator must redirect to /auth/login, not insert

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

with app.app_context():
